This is an individual opinion of each member of the JNA, starting down from a regular soldier all the way up to superior officers. I'm asking him whether, in his opinion, not in accordance with legal practice or laws. I'm asking him whether he, as an average citizen, can differentiate between orders which could constitute a criminal act or be counter to international conventions, and those which do not. Why would it state that at all, then, in the law, that a soldier has the right to refuse an order if he considers it to be a criminal act?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't object to -- to clarify, I don't object to him giving an opinion as to whether he thought it did. I'm objecting to him saying it was or it wasn't. I hope that clarifies my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. From your explanation, Mr. Pisarevic, the Trial Chamber will allow the question, because he -- the witness, as a soldier, and having been acting in that capacity during the events that are being discussed, then he can give his opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A third question: The collection of military weapons from citizens of Bosanski Samac, did that in your opinion constitute a criminal act?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just another question, please: How did Simo Zaric end up as a regular soldier, and which fronts throughout the Republic of Srpska and Bosnia and Herzegovina did he go to, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, Simo Zaric was responsible officer. He was a conscientious officer. He is well qualified to deal with a number of issues. He was a senior officer. As to where he spent his time and on what front lines, you should ask him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that he was at Majevica?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that sounds likely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Glamoc?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bihac?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Krupe?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Krupe. Yes, yes, he was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this concludes my examination-in-chief. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Any other counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no questions for this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Ms. Usher, could I have your assistance in the meantime, please. I have a copy of a certain part of the judgement for the interpreters' booth, so they can follow the translation, please. Cross-examined by Mr. Pantelic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Savic.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My name is Pantelic. I defend Mr. Blagoje Simic. I will ask you a number of questions. Tell me, please, Mr. Savic: Are you a member of any political party?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992, were you a member of any party?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As an educated man, as an officer, as a citizen of Samac, I'm sure you will know from personal experience about which option the SDA and the HDZ were advocating in Samac as concerns the status of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the then Yugoslavia. What did they push for?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These political issues I can only think in terms of what would have been, if something else had been the case, what the party platforms were, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please don't speculate. I'm asking you, as a man who has an average amount of information, specifically: The SDA and the HDZ, did they then advocate an independent Bosnia-Herzegovina? Do you know this from the media or from conversations?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the SDS in favour of remaining within Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In November 1991, was there a plebiscite of the Serbian people?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the subject of that plebiscite remaining within Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please: On the basis of your personal knowledge, on the basis of these views of the SDS, would you characterise the party as nationalistic or rather as national?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would describe the party as a national party of the Serbian people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, Blagoje Simic, prior to the 16th of April, 1992, did he have any contact with the command of the 4th Detachment? Did he make plans concerning an armed takeover in Samac? What do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know of any such thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's your personal knowledge of the following: The municipal SDS of Samac, were they hatching any plans with the 4th Detachment and with the 17th Tactical Group concerning an armed takeover of power or planning a coup to remove the government then in place?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, at that time - I'm talking about April 1992 - was there any such entity as Republika Srpska in existence, or rather, the Republic of the Serbian people within Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, gladly. In April 1992, did the Republika Srpska already exist, or Republic of the Serbian people within Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, in connection with Samac municipality, Bosanski Samac: From the 17th of April, 1992 onwards, you were a military commander. You know what was happening. Samac municipality, in terms of its territory, did it have the same borders as prior to the 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, please tell me: Do you have any knowledge as to how, at that point, and now, what part of the municipality of Samac before the war under Croat control is called? Do you know the name of that particular section of Bosanski Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know of a village which was part of Samac municipality, Domaljevac. It's no longer part of Samac municipality. They call themselves also Bosanski Samac municipality. I know that Prud is no longer part of the municipality, Grebnice. A small part of it did remain on our side, so to speak. Kazi [as interpreted] is no longer with us. That sort of thing. Those villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just for the record. The name of the village mentioned on page 48, line 7, is Bazik, B-A-Z-I-K.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It will be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, Mr. Savic: The SDS in Samac, did they have their own armed unit?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about Samac, but in the village, I do know. We knew about the parties arming themselves. We did know about that, the SDS too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: More specifically, was there an armed unit or formation in the sense of command? What's your personal information concerning that, the HDZ and the SDA, what sort of armed units did they have?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Samac, the SDS did not have any units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please: Do you have any personal information regarding the following: How did the SDA and the HDZ organise themselves in Samac?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did have their own units. Now, what kind of units exactly, what the formations were, which levels of manpower, I don't know, but they did have their own units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I assume you had information on whether they had certain weapons or not.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's the basis for that information?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, I've given you the example of members of the SDA opening fire on a vehicle. I talked about that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but in addition to that.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen individual members walking about town, observing, patrolling, armed people, people who were not part of my detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that the SDS allegedly had an armed unit in one of the villages. Which village was that? Do you know, or is this only an assumption of yours? Do you have any specific information regarding that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there were quite a number of people in the villages who had party affiliations, the SDS, more specifically. They were given weapons. Who gave them weapons and when exactly, I really have no idea, but I know about the organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: More specifically, do you know if there was an SDS armed formation with a commander heading it? Because it was the area of responsibility of the 17th Tactical Group. Where and who was the commander of that alleged SDS armed group, armed unit, in the village?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know a man who was in Batkusa, Mico Banovic, called Mijak. I know that he was a member of the SDS and that he was a commander. But whether that was how he arrived to his position as commander, he was a reserve officer. He was Captain First Class and he was a commander of a unit in Batkusa. That much I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it the 1st Detachment of the 17th Tactical Group where this Mijak was commander?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat? Yes. Yes. It was the 1st Detachment but I must say that the 1st Detachment had its own command in Slatina, and they split up into two groups and Mijak was the commander of that detachment, but only for a brief while. I know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to the 1st and the 4th Detachment that were parts of the 17th Tactical Group, there were three or four other detachments in a were part of the Tactical Group, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were five of them all total, but I'm not sure. Yes, five.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These detachments were headed by JNA officers, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, reserve officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the detachments were headed by officers who were from different political environments, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, you are, after all, a reserve officer. You hold a military rank. During your education, during your military practice, did you have any courses or any programmes concerning the application of international law of war, international humanitarian law, and the Geneva Conventions? Are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will read out to you now two articles from Additional Protocol I of the Geneva Conventions. So tell me, please: You needn't necessarily remember this, but I'd just like to hear whether you agree with the things I'm about to read out to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I mean, what is the importance, what is the relevance of such testimony, whether he agrees or not with the text of Geneva Conventions? They are as they are. I mean, what -- what is the meaning of this? Does the witness agrees with the text of Geneva Convention or not? I really don't see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, can I explain what is the basis?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, what I'm interested in is that to see personal knowledge of this witness with regard to the notion of command responsibility. In this particular articles of Geneva Conventions are dealing with specific issue command responsibility. Because we have facts in dispute here: Who is in charge within the zone of responsibility of one military unit? Whether to some extent are civilian authorities or military authorities. Since this witness was a commander of one of the quite important units with a zone of responsibility in Samac municipality, I think, especially because he's a reserve officer and he knows the provisions of Geneva Conventions, I'd like to clarify certain issues of command responsibility and his personal knowledge about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, this witness hasn't come to court as an expert. He may have military background and all that, but he's here as a fact witness. You can ask him what was happening on the ground. We are interested in the facts. Who was dealing with what. This was a period when so many things were changing, and institutions were being formed so rapidly, as you've heard even the evidence of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So he can tell us as to facts what was happening, who was dealing with what.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Savic, in accordance with the JNA doctrine, we'll agree that this was about the principle of subordination and singleness of command, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the area of responsibility of the 17th Tactical Group, tell me, please: The command, or rather, the commander, Lieutenant Colonel Stevan Nikolic, while he was there, while he was in the area, was he practically responsible for the whole area of responsibility and for all the detachments under his command?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course, it's beyond dispute that his Superior Command was at that point based in Tuzla. It was the Tuzla Corps, commanded by General Savo Jankovic, I think.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Above that corps was the 2nd army, commanded by General Kukanjac.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really know. I wasn't in active service at that point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell us how this functioned. While Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic was the commander of the 17th Tactical Group, in their area of responsibility, were his orders complied with?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only his orders were complied with, no one else's.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic, could he initiate proceedings before military investigative organs if anyone happened to disobey his orders while he was the commander of the 17th Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had every authority and every right to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: Commander Nikolic, did he initiate any proceedings at that time? Did you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have no information regarding that, but I heard about some proceedings that he had initiated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what sort of proceedings those were that he initiated?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm no lawyer myself, so I don't know about these disciplinary measures, but there was something about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. In November, or rather, December 1992 - we're talking about the 2nd Posavina Brigade - there was an incident where a scout was killed in the area of responsibility of the 2nd Posavina Brigade. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible. I remember that someone killed someone else. I remember that. First name, last name, I don't know. I think the person was a scout.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what do you know? Was there a reasonable doubt or grounds to believe that this was committed by the volunteers from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what the stories said that were circulating, but I really don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have information about whether, after this event, whether any proceedings were conducted at the military court in Banja Luka against these perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were stories that some people were arrested, that they were in detention or arrested in Banja Luka, but more than that, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please tell me: Do you remember, in October or November 1992, whether you received from the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska, since at the time you were in the command of the 2nd Posavina Brigade, did you perhaps receive any instructions or guidelines for the criminal prosecution of members of the army of Republika Srpska who committed a criminal act? Do you remember receiving such instructions?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember. I was really just a clerk for operations and training. This is something that perhaps legal staff would know. This is something that they would be aware of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who were in the legal staff in the army?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we did have legal staff. One of them was a lawyer, Mrs. Ana Dragicevic, and the other one I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was she an officer or was she a civilian employed in the military?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was a civilian employed in the military.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in any case, based on this doctrine that we have discussed, any eventual proceedings would be initiated by the commander, i.e., Major Beronja; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that should have been the case, if something like that was required.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just as you, when you were commander of the 4th Detachment of the 17th Tactical Group, were responsible for something that happened in your area of responsibility, and you would be the one who would be submitting a criminal report?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I would inform my Superior Command about that, and they were the ones who had the adequate staff in their section. I would be the one just to pass on a proposal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So practically, whenever you, as the commander of the 4th Detachment, received information about a criminal act being committed or some violation, you would inform your higher command, i.e., the 17th Tactical Group, which would then in turn take the legal steps, the criminal report, court, or whatever other proceedings were necessary; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Dr. Blagoje Simic ever a member of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he ever interfere in the work of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Dr. Blagoje Simic ever send any kind of document, order, instruction, to the 4th Detachment for it to do something?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me when it was formed on the 17th, 18th, and 19th of April, in mid-April, did the Crisis Staff of the Serbian municipality of Samac and Pelagicevo under formation interfere in the work and the area of responsibility of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me whether you, as the 4th Detachment, or you as one of the more prominent people in the 4th Detachment, when the detachment was formed, enjoyed the support of the socio-political community or the municipality, ruled by the SDA, SDS, and the HDZ? Did they then provide support for the formation of the 4th Detachment at the time?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I withdraw my objection. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No political or any other support was necessary in the forming of the unit. Simply, this was carried out by the Ministry of Defence, or the municipal secretariat for the defence, referring to the staffing and all the other issues, and I've already talked about how this was actually carried out in our area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That is very clear to me. I would just like to ask you one more thing. Can we agree that the 4th Detachment was formed based on the principle of voluntary accession, and that those who wished to join volunteered; there was no compulsion to do that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Those who wished to join were given a war assignment, and they remained here in the territory and were given an assignment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So practically --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I believe that the answer of the witness was not properly recorded. He was speaking -- he spoke about first reporting to the ministry and then I don't see this in his answer, here on page 56, line 17. That's those who were to join the Detachment first reported to the Ministry of Defence and then they were sent to the detachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. But we did have that explanation in examination-in-chief, and I think that is sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's sufficient, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So can we agree that the principle that applied in the 4th Detachment regarding its membership was the principle of voluntary membership? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the number varied, but the strength of the detachment ranged from 400 to 450 men; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your answer was not recorded. Could you please repeat that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And regarding the weapons, there were semi-automatic rifles, automatic rifles, mortars, and so on. You've said that earlier.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were no mortars. I did not have any artillery equipment in Samac, just infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any bazookas, Zoljas, or rocket launchers?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was issued later, depending on the type of combat activity, the type of attacks, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since the formation of the detachment, I assume that you also carried out certain kinds of training in military skills, as well as in the application of military law, war law, and so on. Did you do that as part of the training?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, when the war broke out, unfortunately, we did not have enough time to carry out training. However, in contacts with the men, with the officers, it was explained to them that any soldier who had completed training in the JNA had learned the most elementary things and applied them in conditions of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I understand. I'm asking you about the period before the outbreak of the war, so this was in 1991 and early 1992, when you had military training. Did you discuss topics of wartime law and topics like that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Pre- -- in the pre-war period, we did discuss such training. For example, I was deployed in Derventa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm interested in the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We did have target practice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than target practice in the 4th Detachment, you also studied international wartime law and the regulations from the JNA?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We -- even though this is a military topic, we didn't have the conditions, we didn't have the time to do that, and we didn't have experts who would be able to take us through that kind of training, but each soldier who had served their regular duty did learn things about these topics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The components of the Yugoslav People's Army at the time were the army and the TO; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the TO units were under the command of the military unit which would be operating in the relevant area? I'm saying that there was no parallel command, that there was one command for the army and another command for the TO. Could you explain that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Samac there was the municipal TO staff, and it had its own commander and its own organs of command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the commander responsible to, to Colonel Nikolic or somebody else?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had his own Superior Command, municipal staffs and republican staffs. Republic -- municipal staffs, area staffs, and republican staffs. This would be some kind of hierarchy in the TO. But I didn't work in the TO staff. I worked in the secretariat for National Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in any case, the TO units would coordinate their activities with the appropriate military or army unit that was in that territory; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please tell me, regarding events on the night of the 16th and 17th of April: You said that according to you, the 16th was a normal day, just like any other; it wasn't different from any other day. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But on that day, in the evening, around 11.00, you discussed certain tensions and problems in Samac at the command of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's probably that we did. We had these discussions every day. It could have happened in the afternoon, in the morning. I don't remember the exact time when this happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Specifically, I'm interested to know whether Simo Zaric came back from a meeting of the Crisis Staff, of the local commune, on the 16th, and he was pretty upset, and you had a meeting. And did he inform you about what was happening? Now I'm talking about the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't understand what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Could you please come closer to the microphone. Could you bring your chair closer, please.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But at the 4th Detachment command, I assume you did have data available about certain activities on the Croat and Muslim side, that they were arming and that an attack against Samac was being prepared in that period.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Around this time, the 4th Detachment received an ultimatum from the newly founded TO staff to join the TO, practically, of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object. As I understand it, there's no evidence before the Trial Chamber of there being "an ultimatum."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will rephrase that, of course. Maybe it was my slip of the tongue, because I am in defence case, so we have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And Mr. Pantelic, while you're asking this witness questions, please always remember that the armed conflict is admitted by both sides. It's not contentious.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour. I do -- I do agree with that. But the issue here is whether the certain plans of Muslim Croatian side was at that time actual, and what was the response of 4th Detachment and other military units with regard to these alleged plans, of course. So I want to clarify just this relation. Because subsection -- subparagraph 1 of count 1 in the indictment claims that my client, as well as the other accused, are charged with the forcible takeover. So I just want to clarify whether it was a military operation with regard to the preventing incursions of the other side on the territory of Samac or it was, as my learned friend from Prosecution stated, that it was forcible takeover. Simple as that. I will just clarify that, very, very briefly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please tell me if you have any personal knowledge, so we can continue, about there being a request for the 4th Detachment to be placed under the command of the Samac TO at the time. Do you have any information about that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have any information about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me: What were the intelligence sources for you in the 4th Detachment about certain intentions - let me put it that way - of the other side, the enemy side? Did you discuss about what was being prepared at the command? Specifically, I will remind you: Sijekovac, Brod had taken place [as interpreted], and Samac at the time was in a kind of encirclement.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Perhaps question by question, Your Honour. The first question was, what were your intelligence sources?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So specifically, the command of the 4th Detachment, did you discuss, based on certain intelligence data, about the security situation, and if you did discuss such topics, where did these sources -- what were the sources for this, and so on?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that our men in the 4th Detachment were deployed very close to the Republic of Croatia, along the Sava River and the Bosna River, in the direction of Prud. We didn't need any other intelligence work, because we were very close. We knew what the movements of the units were. We had a very small unit which monitored and was carrying out reconnaissance and was suggesting the measures to be taken and reporting back. So there wasn't any kind of intelligence body that dealt with this. Of course, we also received intelligence data at the command, which was processed by Mr. Simo Zaric, and he also proposed the measures to be undertaken. I must say that this was a long time ago. I have forgotten many things. But whatever I remember, I will tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. That's exactly why I wish to remind you now of what Simo Zaric states in his book "Crucified in The Hague." Perhaps this will refresh your memory. He says that at the command of the 17th Tactical Group there were clear outlines of a scenario of a Croat/Muslim coalition attack on Samac at the time. He says that many people even in the 4th Detachment were involved in defending, preparing for the town's defence in a timely manner. Specifically, do you agree with this view expressed by Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. We did have a small unit that was involved in such tasks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, please: Do you know that, in late April, I believe, Simo Zaric put in an appearance, it was a TV show, a programme by Novi Sad TV. They talked about the situation in Samac. Did you see the programme?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I merely heard of it, but I never even talked to him about it. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Be that as it may, this programme was tendered into evidence, this TV show. I will not run this for you now, in order to save time. I'll just read out a section of Simo Zaric's statement from that TV show, because it has been tendered into evidence here. He was asked the following question by the journalist, what was going on in Samac, that sort of thing, and Simo Zaric answered: "Yes, that's true. And we have information that the Crisis Staff, the legally established Crisis Staff, by members of the SDA and the HDZ, had the dirtiest possible intentions towards this people. I can point out to you that we know that they were supposed to perform an operation between the 16th and the 17th, or between the 17th and the 18th of April, which means that this was consistent with our anticipation of the situation, and on the basis of the documents that we have, they were supposed to prepare all the plans and continue their operation to turn this town into a huge tragedy within only 48 hours." Since he was your assistant for intelligence and security, I suppose you would agree with what he said.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you repeated this about six times in a row, perhaps I could agree, but I know that Simo probably got this information through his own channels in different ways, because he was involved in that kind of thing before. So I'm not sure whether I should agree or disagree. This sentence is a rather longish one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the essence of this is about the plans of the SDA and the HDZ, and about a possible attack; do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Finally, in connection with the information we've just discussed: On the basis of all this information, did you practically, on the 16th of April, in the evening, prepare, as a serious military unit, to defend against a possible attack? What did you do? Which steps did you take?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll repeat this to you. The 16th of April was just like the 15th or the 25th of March. No difference. There were no specific preparations on that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Precisely, Mr. Savic. But look at it this way: You have information that a possible attack on Samac is being prepared, and you've just testified to that effect --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... information. He was just agreeing with my colleague that Simo Zaric could have had some informations through his lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes, Mr. Pantelic. What Mr. Lazarevic has pointed out to you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What Mr. Lazarevic appointed out to you is what the witness said in answer to whether or not he had information.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any rate, Mr. Savic, tell us: You said that you at the command discussed the security situation and possible attacks on Samac. My question is: Which steps did you take? Did you reinforce your patrols? Did you issue any orders? What did you do, as a serious military command, on the basis of this really serious information?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We already have the answer to that. The witness said nothing was done on 16th of April it was on ordinary day. This is exactly what the witness said. Asking him again did you make -- he said they didn't do anything, then they didn't do anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. You heard what Mr. Lazarevic has said. If you're talking about the 16th, the witness has already answered that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So is it your submission that all members of the 4th Detachment, on that day, 16th, 17th of April, went home, and to all intents and purposes remained inactive or in bed?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In addition to the patrols --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before the witness answers, you've included the 17th. Did you mean only the 16th?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Or you included both days, 16th and 17th.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In fact, 16 is what I'm interested in now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Meaning on the 16th he had patrols about town?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, just like any other day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me: Who issued the order at 2.00 in the morning on the 17th of April, 1992, so who issued the order to Djordje Dusanovic, member of the 4th Detachment, to cut the phone lines at the post office? Do you have any knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I object. First of all, there was nothing in the testimony of this witness, nor in any testimony we heard before this Tribunal, that there was such an order. Well, actually, there was some mentioning, but a completely different name, in completely different situation. So I really don't understand how the witness can answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: His personal knowledge, Your Honour. Maybe he knows, he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: First of all, he had to ask the witness whether he knows anything, that there was an order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Such an order, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And then if he knows, then who issued the order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because the question was combined. If you split it. Otherwise, if you split it, then the witness can answer whether there was an order, and if there was an order, who issued it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'll do that, Your Honour. By all means.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, Mr. Savic: Did you or anyone else from the command give the order to cut the phone lines at 2.00 in the morning on the 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. My phone lines were down too, so I wouldn't have --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is really something I want to know more about. This is interesting. So the phone lines were down; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a while.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They worked on and off. In the morning, the phone lines were down, and then for two hours it was functioning, and then the lines were down again. If someone had ordered that, I really don't know. I don't think anyone could have ordered that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: Do you have any information regarding the fact as to which members of the 4th Detachment exactly occupied the memorial centre in Samac in the night between the 17th and -- the 16th and the 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The memorial centre, no. The memorial centre and the radio station were taken by the volunteers. Now, if any of the members or any of the patrol members were at the memorial centre, that is possible, but usually the members of the patrol were persons who worked there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the 4th Detachment, were any orders given for the Silo to be taken as one of the vital facilities, key facilities in the town?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no such orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any rate, on the 17th of April, you, the 4th Detachment part of the 17th Tactical Group, acted in cooperation and in coordination with the volunteers from Serbia and with the Serbian police, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In cooperation with the Serbian police and the volunteers, no, by no means, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, then I'm slightly confused by the fact that Simo Zaric, in his book - and he was your assistant and intelligence officer - when speaking about the 17th of April, he said that cooperation with the police and volunteers was necessary for the defence of the town and that it should be coordinated through the command of the 17th Tactical Group. Was there any reason for Simo Zaric, in his book, not to tell the truth concerning coordination?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... page number and the exact quotation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Page 212.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've just read it. He said: "Cooperation with the police and the volunteers is necessary for the defence of the town and will be coordinated through the command of the 17th Tactical Group." If it's Simo Zaric saying this, and --

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If Simo Zaric was the one who said that, it wasn't me saying that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but do you agree?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What should I tell you? Ask him. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a question. Do you agree or not?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cooperation and coordination. I don't agree with the volunteers --

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- because we had nothing to do with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: This book you are quoting from has never been placed before on record, has it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Not yet, Your Honour. Maybe -- maybe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have it, since --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- our learned friends can help us with that, because they are in possession of this book. Whether it was translated or not, I'm not so sure, but during the break maybe I can clarify that with them, because it's quite a large book.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If Mr. Pantelic is referring to Mr. Zaric's book "Crucified in The Hague" first edition 1999, the Prosecution does in fact have a copy of it and translated and we are more than happy to tender it into evidence when we have copies. I assume Mr. Pantelic has a copy there himself which he could show to the witness if necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because if it's being referred to in evidence, then it had better be tabled.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe, as my learned friend just mentioned, they will be willing to tender into evidence. In fact, I've finished with this small portion and these events, so I will not explore deeply the issue from this book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. But we still require it to be on record.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Perhaps the Prosecution have said they have copies, it can be tendered later.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's quite lengthy, several hundred pages. We'll have to have copies made. I don't know whether we could have it done this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. What I was asking about: You have it translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's why I said at a later stage, since you're not ready for copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If it please the court.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do apologise. I'm feeling terribly, I have a serious flu, hopefully not Hong Kong type, but I have to get my medicine. Could we have an early -- to break now? Because I have to get this medicine, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. We shall take an early break and resume our proceedings at 12.45.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We shall continue our proceedings under Rule 15 bis, paragraph A, as Judge Lindholm is not able to be with us. Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, before the break, Mr. Savic, we spoke about the events related to the key buildings and facilities in Samac. Tell me, please, now that we've been talking about the type of radio station RUP 2: What is its range? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not a communications officer myself. Maybe it was RUP 12. But really, I'm not an expert. I'm sorry. That's communications. It was a piece of communications equipment. What its range was, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm simply asking you because experts say that RUP 2 has a range of -- between one and a half and two kilometres. That's why I didn't understand you were referring to that type of equipment.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please believe me, I have no idea the number, the range. I was not a communications officer. That was down to them to know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: The 17th Tactical Group was involved in certain military defensive operations from the 17th of April onwards, because the enemies were attacking. Do you know that the air force was also involved in the Samac theatre of war? Did the air force also give support to the 17th Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in Samac. I know that for a fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, however, since you're an experienced officer: Did the commander of the 17th Tactical Group have the possibility at his disposal to call in the air force?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the 17th Tactical Group would not have had the authority, the mandate, to do that. Maybe if he tried asking for help, somewhere higher up the chain of command, but I don't know if he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you have any information regarding the fact that the staff of General Kukanjac, in Sarajevo, was informed that the 17th Tactical Group, in the night between the 16th and 17th of April, took part actively in the operations that took place in Samac? Do you have any information regarding that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told my learned colleague Mr. Pisarevic some things about the proclamation by the 4th Detachment. You just commented on the heading and the signature. And I would like to talk about that in more detail with you, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Exhibit D28/4, please, ter. [Interpretation] I don't know. [In English] This document on the ELMO and then so that the other co-accused could follow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it's not a problem for you, Mr. Savic, I don't know whether you are able to see it on the screen. If you find it a little difficult, then perhaps you can read it directly from the ELMO when I ask you questions relating to the document. On page 2, the first paragraph that talks about the detachment calling on all honourable people to join and to respect the decrees of its command on the organisation of life and work and the preservation of peace and order in Bosanski Samac, as a member of the command or the deputy commander of the 4th Detachment actively participated in drawing up this document; is this true?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's partially true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't understand you. Did you say partially true?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partially true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please explain that. What do you mean, partially, that you participated partially?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the following way: Radovan Antic, the commander, and his deputy, or assistant, Simo Zaric, tried, and the command accepted this, in this way to try to secure the situation, to return things to a normal framework, to try to get people to join the army. This is what happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you wholly agree with this proclamation. This is what I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of the objectives of this proclamation is to explain to the citizens of Samac that law and order in Samac would be preserved and that they will be re-established. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was an attempt to establish law and order, an attempt. One of the ways we thought that this would be the way to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also wished to strengthen the 4th Detachment and you called on people to join the 4th Detachment, to become its members and to receive weapons legally; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell me: How do you interpret this paragraph directly below, on page 2, where it says that the detachment will have no mercy for provocators who are assisted by international fascism and who are now calling for fratricide and so on? First, please tell me: What would the detachment do, what kind of steps would it take against these provocators?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our options were weak. This was just a plan of wishes in an attempt to improve the situation in the town and to make the life of the citizens easier. That's all. I'm not a literary critic so that I could give you assessment or qualifications in the political sense or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that, when asked by my colleague Mr. Pisarevic, that you had certain orders, the collection of arms, and so on, and the other activities, deployment on the embankment and so on. Please tell me: As part of your plans, the military plans to calm the situation, did you also work to isolate those persons who possessed weapons or could have been possible provocators in relation to the positions of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no such plans, nor did we do anything like that, except for the collection of weapons. This was carried out. But as far as isolation is concerned, this was not undertaken at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any case, you, as an experienced officer, when you found out that there were armed elements who were jeopardising the security of the detachment and of civilians, would such a measure be justified in those conditions?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was for us to inform the higher command, and they would be the ones to resolve these problems. Other than the ordered activities and measures, we had no other authority to carry anything out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But my question was: Would this be a justified measure if you had knowledge that there were people who were in possession of weapons? This is what I'm asking you. Would this be a justified measure?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps it would be. Yes, I think that it would be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would a justified measure also be that those people who had certain plans or possessed weapons give statements, that statements be taken from these people in a legal manner?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in any case, this would be justified.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if there were founded suspicions, would it then be appropriate for those people to be processed before the authorised courts? Would that be justified?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... question, but it is not quite clear to me whether he was referring, the witness, as a member of the detachment or this is just his general opinion about these situation if appear certain situation it would be an appropriate measure. Would that measure be undertaken, but the 4th Detachment or someone else. This is not quite clear the line of questioning and the answers that the witness gave was. Was it related to the detachment or just generally?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It appears to just have been general questions, because there was no particularisation [Realtime transcript read in error "particular authorisation"] as to whether or not you were asking the witness in his capacity as a member of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Savic, you, as a reserve officer and a man of certain experience, all of these things that we were saying about would these be justified measures, also in the case of the 4th Detachment, which was a legitimate military unit?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, please, could you please repeat the question? I'm not sure if I understood it properly. So will you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Can we agree that the 4th Detachment, as a regular unit of the JNA and part of the 17th Tactical Group, in accordance with the standards, military standards, was obliged, in case of armed rebellion or anything like that, had the legal option, as well as the possibility to take statements from such persons and initiate criminal proceedings and process these people before the responsible courts?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: My objection, Your Honours, is to Mr. Pantelic seeking a legal opinion from someone who is clearly not legally qualified to give an opinion as to the legal - what's the word - basis for 4th Detachment taking any measures against people in those circumstances. He can say what the 4th Detachment did, but not offer the Chamber legal advice.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, I was -- my question was just limited to his personal knowledge in capacity of the Captain First Class and then deputy commander, with regard to the -- these general notions, specifically related to the military legislation, not more. Not as a high expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Still more grounded down as to what actually happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before he answers, I note that my intervention was not properly recorded. I didn't say no particular authorisation. I said no particularisation. The witness can go ahead and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're talking about the 4th Detachment, and based on your military knowledge and experience, would these be justified procedures and actions to in some way prevent the danger from certain groups which were armed and could inflict some harm?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Weapons were already taken from such groups, and in Samac, I have no information that any of them were left once the weapons were collected. But what do I think in the event that there was some such groups? Perhaps, yes. Only to inform the Superior Command, nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as this proclamation, the 4th Detachment stood by it and never had any reason to abandon it partially or in its entirety; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you that - and I know this now, and I knew it earlier also - that this could not be implemented. I wasn't in the situation and I didn't have the possibility of translating it into action. If we did have the opportunity, had we been able to really do something to prevent the conflict from breaking out, well, that would have been something good. But this was a kind of attempt and nothing more than that, to help the people, and this is what I was talking about at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How would you describe the 4th Detachment, as far as its numerical strength and arming? Was this a small unit or did it have a certain weight? How would you describe it?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 4th Detachment, first of all, was of mixed composition, and it operated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you just hold on? This question has been amply answered in examination-in-chief by the witness. He explained about the 4th Detachment, its various units, numbers, and things like that. Please let's not repeat examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In terms of numbers and units it's okay but I just want to elicit from this witness his personal position with regard to the -- in military sense, of power of this 4th Detachment. Because actually he said prior to that that 4th Detachment was some kind of, you know, unit without any particular power or to prevent or to organise. So that was the basis for my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's what I'm saying, that he has already explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regarding the 4th Detachment, you explained to my learned friend, Mr. Pisarevic, already the weapons that it had in terms of numbers. But please tell me: On page 1 of this proclamation, the first paragraph -- as the 4th Detachment, you had taken upon yourself the responsibility for freedom, peace, order, work, and normal life and the dignity of every man in Samac. Could you please explain to the Trial Chamber, Mr. Savic?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This sentence --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. The question is coming now. Why a detachment with 400 members, who are well armed with automatic and semi-automatic rifles, was unable to implement the first part of this proclamation? Can you explain that to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already explained that, but I will repeat myself. The 4th Detachment, according to its manpower and the way they were coming to the detachment, it was first of all 20 and then 40 and then a hundred people. So this was a process that was ongoing. The people kept arriving. Some of them were out in the field, and so on. We didn't have the option, and I will say it again. This was just a wish. It was just a wish, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you, as deputy commander of the detachment, noticed that there was looting, that there were certain abuses and certain criminal acts being perpetrated, did you personally inform your Superior Command, the command of the 17th Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally did not, because I wasn't the commander. Once I became the commander, it was my duty to report back to them. In those initial few days, it was Radovan Antic who was in command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you became the commander of the 4th Detachment, there were no such occurrences in Samac?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were plenty of such occurrences.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you inform your Superior Command?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did the Superior Command do in this regard?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At meetings, Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic informed us that, together with the MUP of Samac, there was an agreement, there were attempts to prevent that, to reduce the number of such occurrences, that this wasn't going to lead to anything. This is something that Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic informed us about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So nothing was done?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I, nor the army, did not deal with such things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But during the time that you were commander of the 4th Detachment, what was going on in the area of the detachment's responsibility? Was everything normal or was it chaos?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was only concerned about having the army in its proper place. What was happening in town was in the jurisdiction of the MUP. These were my orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. The last paragraph on the first page of this proclamation states -- what did you say? My colleagues tell me that in the previous answer -- who was at the head of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stevan Todorovic, called Stiv.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Savic, the last paragraph on page 1, that this whole situation engendered practically an armed all peoples' detachment as an expression of the power of all the people. So in a way, you informed the public that the 4th Detachment, by difficult and honourable fighting, established control over all vital points and facilities in town. What are all of these key facilities? Could you please tell us what they are.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about the key facilities in the town, because I spent many years there, as far as security for those buildings and institutions. Security was provided by people who worked there in those companies, mainly elderly people, retirees. They tried to preserve that. I think even if a military unit had been in place, it would have been very difficult to prevent that. But the military were not in a position to engage in that, because we were supposed to occupy the defence lines of the town itself. That was our remit and those were our orders, and that's exactly what we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did tell me a moment ago that everything in this public announcement proclamation is true. Why are you now denying this particular section? Can you please explain that.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that everything was true. I said this was merely an attempt, and I would say it's rather a waste of energy, eventually turned out to be. We didn't have the power, we didn't have the resources to do this. We merely wished to help the citizens of Samac, and that was all, and that was also all that I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I'm asking you, in connection with this particular paragraph, Mr. Savic -- you can read it yourself: The 4th Detachment established control over all vital points and key institutions in the town. Please explain what's unclear about this, it's only logical that you would have the same position as does the armed force. I'm asking you about which facilities those were that you had placed under control. That's all I'm asking you. Because that's what the public announcement states. I have no reason to doubt that.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you about this announcement and what I thought it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is not true?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had no power, no ability, and no conditions to secure this. We left it to the civil authorities, and they were supposed to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This announcement, when this announcement was being drawn up, did you at the command of the 4th Detachment discuss any participation of the SDS and Blagoje Simic in these aims set forth by the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We read the announcement in times of war. It was a cursory reading. Commander Radovan Antic decided that Simo should distribute this announcement, copies of this announcement, to Radio Samac, and that it should be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your capacity as commander of the 4th Detachment, in the meantime, you tried to preserve some law and order in the area of responsibility of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you try to create havoc in the area of responsibility of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. We operated on the fringes of the area, carrying out military operations. We suffered casualties every single day. We were under fire. But we had to preserve those lines of defence. As far as law and order in the town itself, that was the responsibility of the organs of authority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which specific steps did you take when Lugar attacked your commanders? You at the command, which steps did you take to punish this perpetrator?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We merely informed Commander Nikolic, and nothing else. And then he took steps, in coordination with organs of government. He asked Radovan to stay on and everything else. But I've told you about that already, didn't I?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: Did you also report volunteers who had been arresting members of the 4th Detachment? Did you report them to the Superior Command?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever we found out about, we reported everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, then: What was the reason for you not to arrest the Crisis Staff of the Serbian municipality in its entirety, Samac and Pelagicevo? Did you not have that kind of order from Colonel Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that a group of volunteers, after the corridor was broken through by the 1st Krajina Corps, that the group of volunteers, Crni, Lugar, and the other people, were arrested by the 1st Krajina Corps?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether arrested or not, yeah, but they were arrested. I did hear about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge of the fact that Dr. Blagoje Simic and Savo Popovic, as representatives of the civilian authorities, contacted the bodies in the 1st Krajina Corps in order to inform them about certain illegal occurrences and in order to appeal to the army to help, to suppress this? Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic, on account of all the crimes committed by Lugar, ever initiated any proceedings against him before military organs? You were a commander of one of his detachments. At meetings, at the command meetings, did you receive any such information? Did you learn about that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know of anything like that. Maybe proceedings were initiated, but not that I know of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You commented on this document relating to the 13 signatories, the command members of the brigade. This is the document -- this is the report you discussed with my colleague Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Ms. Usher, could we have P127, please. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're about to be shown this document, but meanwhile, did you have any personal knowledge as to when this document was discussed or reviewed, and when was it made public, in a manner of speaking? Were there any initiatives within the framework of the brigade to convene an interim meeting of the Municipal Assembly of Samac?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Frankly, I can't remember. I can't remember. Maybe there was something like that, but not that I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you agree with me if I say, if I put it to you that the motive for the writing of this report was the desire of a certain structure within the 2nd Posavina Brigade to carry out a coup against the civilian bodies of authority and to take over power? Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Shall we then agree that the signatories of this document, or rather, this report, wanted to draw other people's attention to certain other illegal activities that were going on and to have proceedings initiated against its perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do agree with that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, then. I assume that, on page 5 of this document, this is halfway down the page. I'll read it to you. We've discussed this before. This is about the killing of the scout. We spoke about this a while ago. It's part of the report. You see this section where he says: "The responsibility of Crni and his people surrounding the arrest, maltreatment, and killing of a scout from the 1st Krajina Brigade is being investigated because there are proceedings under way against these same people." And then further on it states, towards the bottom of the same paragraph: "After all, the media are already publishing news about this incident, so you can monitor the developments through the media." Will you agree with me that this report influenced the relevant military organs to initiate proceedings against certain persons suspected of having committed certain crimes?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe so, but I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The assistant for legal affairs in the brigade, would he have been in charge of filing charges?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Down towards the bottom of the page 5, the report also contains the following information. There is an admission that Crni and his people were, for the first time arrested, and that he had compromised his reputation and his position, and so on and so forth, towards the bottom of the page. So at that meeting at the brigade command -- that's the last sentence, Mr. Savic, and we knew exactly what he and the likes of him would happen to them when they were first arrested. More specifically, what I wish to tell you is: At that meeting, you knew that for the first time Crni and his people had been arrested. You did know that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We had heard about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm asking you now is: Who was it that arrested him? The civilian police or organs of military security?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. On page 3 of this report, the first paragraph. They are speaking about the crime committed by Lugar at Crkvina. "Both the Yugoslav and world media covered this, and the crime was attributed to Serbian fighters from our municipality," the document states, "whereby a large share of collective blame is assumed which will only be clarified and accounted for after the war." Mr. Savic, if there were proceedings that had been initiated against Lugar and his group for -- because of the killing of the scout and other robberies or whatever it was that had happened there, tell me: What was the reason for proceedings not to be initiated before the court in Banja Luka in relation to the murder in Crkvina?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... quite obvious from his previous answer. How could he know why Lugar wasn't arrested, or arrested, or who arrested him, and why the procedure did take place or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: He signed this document, Your Honour. He signed. He was in the command, in the high command of the 2nd Posavina Brigade. So I just want to know his -- what he personally did at that time in that capacity, as a member of command of 2nd Posavina Brigade, with regard to the information that he shared with the other members of the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
