utterances.text: Yes. And that's all right. But we must have in mind that when Lugar did the crime in Crkvina, 2nd Posavina Brigade haven't even existed. So in this capacity, how could he know something like that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Because -- I will ask a few questions and I will establish how it might be possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, you are simply going around and around about this issue, wasting time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will go directly to the issue, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you've already told me, Mr. Savic, that before the military court in Banja Luka, proceedings had been initiated for the murder of this scout. You did hear about that, didn't you? That's what the discussion in this report is based on.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I had no idea whether anyone was sentenced, whether any proceedings had been initiated. I really don't know. Maybe so, but I don't know. I should go through the report thoroughly again in order to perhaps recall something. But I didn't know about arrests, who arrested whom and where and what and why. I really have no idea about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I fully understand you. However, there are proceedings under way against this group of volunteers before the military court in Banja Luka, and I just read this out to you from this report. I'm asking you: Regardless of the fact whether they were part of the army of Republika Srpska at that point, and you will agree with me that war crimes -- that no statute of limitation applies to war crimes. You do agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first part of what you said, yes, I do agree. But the second part, Lugar and his team, they were not part of the army. These are two different issues. I think that's quite a difference there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's keep it simple. No statute of limitation for war crimes?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do understand that perfectly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 13 signatories of this report, you all knew that Lugar was the perpetrator of the crime in Crkvina, and you knew very well that Lugar was being prosecuted by the military court in Banja Luka for the murder of the scout. Tell me, please, I'm asking you personally, you personally,

utterances.speaker: MR. SAVIC
utterances.text: Why did you not inform the military prosecutor about the fact that you had information on the basis of this report that Lugar had committed the crime in Crkvina, you personally? Or maybe you did inform the military prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I don't know who informed or failed to inform. That was not part of my remit. It was not in my job description. I was merely a clerk in my department, and I had no authority, no power and no need to do that. Now, as to who actually did it, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you personally, although you knew about it, failed to inform the relevant military prosecutor about this?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This had nothing to do with me. It's as simple as that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, I think the witness has explained sufficiently.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, please, in connection with the volunteers who arrived in Batkusa: Can we then agree that they, their arrival had been organised by the JNA and that they were shipped there in JNA military helicopters?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who the helicopters belonged to, I have no idea, whether the JNA took part, I don't know. I only know that those people were not part of my unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: In fact, in examination-in-chief, the witness had explained this. In fact, I remember Judge Williams's question about them using JNA helicopters.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The next question is related to this previous one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Savic, those volunteers, you saw them about town, didn't you? Which part of Serbia? Which town were they from? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't even know their names. How on earth should I know where they came from? They kept using nicknames. I did speak about that yesterday, if I remember correctly. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was Stevan Nikolic from? Which town in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may go wrong on this one, but I think around Kragujevac, Krusevac, that area. I think Kragujevac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the assault battalion established, whose first commander was Josic, I believe, wasn't he? When was that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when, but I know that Josic was the commander of the Assault Battalion. But I was not a member of the brigade at that time. I wasn't in Samac. I don't know the details surrounding this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was his assistant or deputy Colonel Popovic, known as Pop?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... small misunderstanding in transcript. Here on page 89, line 13, I believe that the rank of this gentleman, Popovic, was not properly translated. He wasn't actually a colonel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So what is the correct rank?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the deputy of Josic? What was his rank?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was Lieutenant Bogdanovic. Excuse me Bogdan Popovic, called Pop. He was a lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see, personally, any order of the Crisis Staff to volunteers in the sense of carrying out a military operation or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you ever see any orders by the commander of the 17th Tactical Group to volunteers, in connection with combat operations?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Usher. I've finished with this document, with P127.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Today you spoke about a meeting at the heating plant, related to the appointment of Djurdjevic, the dismissal, and so on and so forth. Tell me, please: Well, yes, to make it more accurate. We're talking about the meeting at the heating plant where allegedly Djurdjevic was dismissed, or removed, replaced. That's what I'm talking about. Tell me, please: Did you know that Colonel Djurdjevic had been appointed by a Superior Command by Colonel Dencic, as commander of the 1st Posavina Brigade, based in Brcko thereafter? Did you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Colonel Djurdjevic did go to Brcko and that he was commander of the 1st Posavina Brigade. Now, on whose orders, I'm not sure. The command, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you will agree with me when I say that due to the principle of subordination, when a Superior Command adopts a decision or issues an order, there's no discussing that, is there?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Furthermore, did you know that, according to the regulations valid for the army of Republika Srpska at that time, the regulations in force, the appointment of brigade commanders is the responsibility of the Minister of Defence? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but no, it wasn't the Minister of Defence who actually appointed them. The corps would nominate candidates and then the list would be sent to the General Staff, and then from then on, whether it was forwarded to the minister or not, I really don't know. But the proposal could have gone from the brigade directly to the General Staff or the minister, up the chain of command, in a manner of speaking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any rate, those were the superior bodies, the Superior Command, the ministry. We do agree on that, don't we?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you personally know whether there is any paper, document, decision, in writing, by the Crisis Staff, concerning the removal of Colonel Djurdjevic? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I know absolutely nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, in view of the fact that the 4th Detachment was set up in the beginning of January 1992, do you know that the presidency of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia adopted a decision to place all volunteer units under the command of the relevant military commands? Were you aware of this decision?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could this be clarified, please? My learned friend Mr. Pantelic has just referred to a decision of the presidency of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, but without saying when, so I think it's quite relevant to the question asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In fact, I mentioned that, but probably it was not in the transcript. I will clarify that. I said that this order -- that this order was issued in December 1991, just for the record. Your Honour, could I have just a few moments to reorganise my questions? Because I'm very near to the close of my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can you do it quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Just a few seconds, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Savic. Did you know that security bodies or organs across military units have the authority and the right to prevent a civilian person caught while committing a crime from fleeing such crimes as envisaged punishment of 15 or more years? Did you know about these measures as applied in the army?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I think you should ask them about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you, as an officer, as a commander of a detachment. Your security assistant was a qualified person in that sense. It's in that context that I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll tell you: Simo did not have the authority to arrest anyone, to prosecute anyone. He only had the authority to report to his Superior Command, and that was that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. You spoke about the crime in Crkvina and how after that, Simo Zaric went to Belgrade, travelled to Belgrade, on official duty. Can you please tell us why it wasn't his superior, Mr. Simeunovic, his direct superior, who travelled to Belgrade? Because you were talking about reporting to the Superior Command always.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... first my colleague should establish whether this witness has personal knowledge about why this man or not the other man went to Belgrade, and then ask him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The question doesn't simply make sense, because the witness did explain this in examination-in-chief. The question doesn't make sense. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will clarify that. Maybe I was not so precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, please, Mr. Savic: It is an agreed fact that Maksim Simeunovic was the Superior Commander of Simo Zaric, I'm talking about the Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you personally as the commander of the 4th Detachment, did you know the reason why Maksim Simeunovic was not the one who went to Belgrade to speak to the security organs there but rather Simo Zaric. Did Simo Zaric ever provide an explanation for that? Did you talk about this?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How in the world am I supposed to know who should go to Belgrade, whether Simo or Maksim Simeunovic? Whoever the commander says should go will go. Simo Zaric only phoned and said, informed me about that. That was all his duty was about. That's all he had to do. He told me: Commander, I'm going to Belgrade. I have received orders to go to Belgrade. I'll be back in a couple of days. And he was indeed back in a couple of days and that was that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I put it to you, finally, that you, as the commander of the 4th Detachment, were responsible for prosecuting the perpetrators of the crime at Crkvina, will you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had nothing in the world to do with me. It was outside my area of responsibility, to begin with. I had nothing to do with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not saying that you did have anything to do with that, but would you agree with my statement, my submission, that your responsibility was to start or initiate proceedings before military organs?

utterances.speaker: JOVO SAVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How should I be doing that? That wasn't part of my job.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've finished with the cross-examination of this witness. [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Savic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It appears there's only two minutes left, Your Honour. Would it be appropriate to start tomorrow rather than attempt something today and not get very far at all?
